problem_summary.summary: Return the input singly linked list sorted in ascending order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: the head of a singly linked list. Return its sorted head; ListNode is provided by the judge.
constraints: Follow-up: O(n log n) time and O(1) auxiliary memory

brute_force.explanation: Copy node values into an array, sort the array with the standard library, then write the sorted values back into the existing nodes. This provides a simple baseline but uses linear extra storage.
brute_force.correctness_idea: The array contains every list value exactly once. Sorting it orders that complete multiset, and writing values back in list order yields the required ascending sequence without changing the list length.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n log n) for sorting the collected values, with O(n) traversal and rewrite work.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary space for the copied values; existing list nodes are reused.

optimized.explanation: Use bottom-up merge sort on linked-list runs of widths 1, 2, 4, and so on. Each pass splits adjacent runs, merges them by relinking nodes, and avoids both value storage and recursive call-stack space.
optimized.correctness_idea: A merge of two sorted runs is sorted and contains exactly their nodes. Each pass merges adjacent runs of equal width, producing sorted runs twice as long; once the width covers the list, the entire list is sorted.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n log n) — each bottom-up pass processes every node once and there are O(log n) passes.
optimized.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space apart from a fixed number of pointers and one dummy node; the algorithm is iterative and relinks the input nodes.

steps.condition: Both runs contain at most one node and are individually sorted.
steps.action: Relink the merged pair as [1,4], then merge [3] and [2] as [2,3].
Repeatedly choose the smaller head and relink nodes in order 1, 2, 3, 4.

steps.condition: width is no longer less than length.
steps.action: Return the dummy head's next node.

edge_cases.handling: Returned immediately because it is already sorted.
split returns null or a shorter run, and merging accepts either run ending first.
The <= comparison consistently takes from the left run first, preserving all values and stable order.
